scope: Proposition 7.4 (Scalar comparison) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 50. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose a set of productive modular-good paths has probability at least τ, with log(1/τ) pre bounded, and each has a specified pre-cost slice. Consider bounded scores depending on site and auxiliary labels. Assume that, after partitioning into pre-count many pre-cost slices, each score is uniformly approximable at the required pre accuracy, both on actual path arguments and on the joint support of K, by the same menu of bounded site functions. A bounded number of successive increases of these pre bounds is allowed. Then, outside a set of paths smaller than the productive probability, the actual scalar averages and their K integrals differ by an arbitrarily prescribed pre-small error. This holds simultaneously for a pre-count menu of scores and for path-dependent slice choices. At active layers it also holds after multiplying a score by the no-bad-flag indicator. It is valid either for normalized slice averages or with full-box mass retained, paying the explicit slice fractions. The budget is warm for passive uses and cold pre otherwise.
